question: What Is the Au Cheval Burger?
quick_answer: The Au Cheval cheeseburger is a diner-style burger made with thin, griddled patties, American cheese, dijonnaise and pickles on a toasted bun. Even the "single" comes with two patties, and you can add thick-cut bacon and a fried egg, which is what Au Cheval's name refers to. It costs about $20 on our latest menu check. Chicago's West Loop original has long been walk-in only, with waits of one to three hours, while the New York location in Tribeca takes reservations on Resy.

body.heading: What's on the burger
body.text: Au Cheval's burger follows the classic diner style: thin patties griddled hot and fast so they get a crisp edge and stay juicy, then layered with American cheese, dijonnaise and pickles on a toasted bun. The menu's "single" actually has two patties, and the "double" adds another, which is why some people describe it as triple-stacked. The most popular way to order it adds thick-cut bacon and a fried egg on top. In French, "au cheval" refers to a dish served with an egg on top.

body.heading: How much it costs
body.text: On our latest menu check, the single cheeseburger is about $19.99 and the double is about $20.99, with bacon and an egg costing extra. Most people add a side of fries, about $9.99, or the crispy potatoes topped with a farm egg, about $15.99. Prices differ slightly between Chicago and New York. See our Au Cheval menu for the full list.

body.heading: Why it's so famous
body.text: Chef Brendan Sodikoff opened Au Cheval in Chicago's West Loop in 2012 as part of his Hogsalt restaurant group. The burger quickly picked up national praise, including from the Food Network, which called it one of the best in the country, and it has stayed on Chicago best-burger lists ever since. The diner also built a following for its fried bologna sandwich and honey-fried chicken.

body.heading: The wait and reservations in Chicago
body.text: The Chicago restaurant, at 800 W Randolph St., has long been first come, first served, and its own website says it doesn't take reservations. Waits of one to three hours are common, especially on weekends, and many people put their name in and wait at nearby bars on Randolph Street. In September 2026, Resy reported that Au Cheval had started taking limited reservations for parties of four, so check Resy before you go. It's open from 10 a.m. to 11:15 p.m. Monday through Saturday and until 10:15 p.m. on Sunday.

body.heading: Au Cheval in New York
body.text: Au Cheval opened its New York location in March 2019 at 33 Cortlandt Alley in Tribeca, an 85-seat room serving the same burger. Within weeks it began taking reservations on Resy to cut down on three-hour lines. Tables open up to 21 days ahead, with new dates released at 9 a.m. Eastern, and walk-ins can sometimes get seats at the counter.
